content: All vaccines included in the adult immunization schedule are covered by the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program, with the exception of the pneumococcal 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) and the zoster vaccines (RZV and ZVL). For more information, you can visit the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program website or contact them during their operating hours, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. The 2020 United States Adult Immunization Schedule includes recommendations for the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. Routine HPV vaccination is advised for all adults up to the age of 26 years. The vaccination series can consist of either two or three doses, depending on the age at which the individual begins the vaccination or their specific health conditions. For individuals who are 15 years or older at the time of their initial HPV vaccination, a three-dose series is required. The doses should be administered at 0, 1–2, and 6 months. The minimum intervals between doses are as follows: 4 weeks between the first and second doses, 12 weeks between the second and third doses, and 5 months between the first and third doses. If any dose is administered earlier than the recommended interval, it should be repeated. For individuals aged 9 through 14 years at the time of their initial HPV vaccination who received only one dose or two doses less than 5 months apart, an additional dose is required to complete the series. For individuals aged 9 through 14 years at the time of their initial HPV vaccination who received two doses at least 5 months apart, the HPV vaccination series is considered complete, and no additional doses are necessary.
